Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-0-transcribe-medium-0289", "row_sha256": "dbec5db6cbfe73b489d108d78e6894ed8a71e7016e61cfd52dab93810c6465be", "mode": "/transcribe", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Remove true hesitation and accidental restarts. Apply explicit corrections to the final stated intent. Preserve meaningful filler-like words and unfinished thoughts. Apply clearly spoken punctuation and list cues. Keep the supplied language.", "input": "um hi mara i wanted to check in about the seed exchange at the library next saturday because the room booking has changed a little and i thought you should know before you print the signs well i spoke with dan at the front desk yesterday and he said we can still use the meeting room but we need to bring our own folding table for the packets i asked if the side entrance would be open and he said uh-huh it should be unlocked by nine though the main doors do not open until ten actually the gardening club is arriving at nine thirty so i can meet them outside and carry the boxes in like we have beans calendula and two kinds of tomato seeds but i am still waiting to hear whether priya is bringing the herbs the labels are in the blue envelope on my porch and the envelopes for the seed stories are in the same bag please tell people to write the variety and the year on each packet if they know it i will bring tea and paper cups but could you bring the small sign-in notebook if the room feels crowded we can spread the packets along the windowsill instead of making a second table see you saturday and thanks for helping make the exchange easy for new gardeners", "output": "Hi Mara, I wanted to check in about the seed exchange at the library next Saturday because the room booking has changed a little, and I thought you should know before you print the signs. Well, I spoke with Dan at the front desk yesterday, and he said we can still use the meeting room, but we need to bring our own folding table for the packets. I asked if the side entrance would be open, and he said, “Uh-huh, it should be unlocked by nine,” though the main doors do not open until ten. Actually, the gardening club is arriving at nine thirty, so I can meet them outside and carry the boxes in. Like, we have beans, calendula, and two kinds of tomato seeds, but I am still waiting to hear whether Priya is bringing the herbs. The labels are in the blue envelope on my porch, and the envelopes for the seed stories are in the same bag. Please tell people to write the variety and the year on each packet if they know it. I will bring tea and paper cups, but could you bring the small sign-in notebook? If the room feels crowded, we can spread the packets along the windowsill instead of making a second table. See you Saturday, and thanks for helping make the exchange easy for new gardeners."}]
